result:
Both round-1 defects are genuinely fixed, and I verified them independently rather than taking the submission's word.

## Resolved

**[1.1] blocking → fixed.** `preamble.txt` now declares `amsmath`. I tested it the way that actually matters: generating the wrapper preamble by `cat`-ing the *shipped* `preamble.txt` rather than hand-writing one — the exact mistake that caused the round-1 failure. Result: exit 0, zero errors, one page.

I didn't accept the worker's claim that the package set is now minimal and sufficient. Dropping each declared package in turn:

```
without amsmath   -> exit 1 | ! Undefined control sequence.  (l.4  $64\text)
without booktabs  -> exit 1 | ! Undefined control sequence.  (l.17 \toprule)
without float     -> exit 1 | ! LaTeX Error: Unknown float option `H'.
```

All three are load-bearing, none superfluous. And none of those failures was a spurious file-not-found — no `neg_*.log` contains "not found", and the test-dir `answer.tex` diffs clean against the shipped one.

**[1.2] minor → fixed properly.** Rather than softening the wording, the worker made the claim true: `check.py` now computes the 128 KB case and asserts `size_c * 2 == size`, plus the virtual-pages cross-check I raised. I re-ran it and diffed stdout against the verbatim block quoted at `submission.md:99-106` — byte-identical.

**No regression.** `answer.tex` is byte-identical to round 1, so the mathematics I verified independently still stands. I rendered the compiled PDF and read it: table typesets 16 / 14 / 30 under the original headers, caption LaTeX-numbered, A/B/C labelled, both pros and both cons legible. `lint_output.py` exits 0; R5 and namespacing clean.

## Remaining (minor, noted not blocking)

**[2.1]** `submission.md` lines 64-65 and 88 describe a negative control at `build/neg.tex`. It doesn't exist — `ls build/` shows only the master files, and `find` turns up no `neg.*` anywhere in the playground. I flag it because it's the same class as [1.2]: describing an artifact that overstates what's on disk. It isn't blocking, because the claim it was meant to support is true and I verified it twice myself. Nothing in `OUTPUT` depends on it.

The deliverable is correct, compiles against exactly its declared packages, and answers all three sub-parts. My only remaining objection is playground-side bookkeeping.

VERDICT: PASS
